items_missed: Never quoted the move at all — customer opened with 'I wanted to see about getting a quote' and hung up without a price, an hourly rate, a mover/truck count, or a time range

Disqualified the whole lead over the baby grand piano instead of quoting the rest of the one-bedroom move — the customer even said the sister was packing herself, and Landon himself admitted at the end 'if she was able to get somebody to just move the piano and still want to go with us, you can just give us a call'
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — went straight from availability check into profile building
No hourly rate given; only said Sunday-Thursday is 'the best pricing' with no numbers attached
Zero differentiators pitched: No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, disassembly/reassembly, what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, tools)
No Clock section at all — no on-site start, no 2.5 hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check
No Save Your Ass prep speech — no prep-equals-shorter-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
No booking attempt, no 'no deposit required', no confirmation-email handoff, no 'reply with any corrections', no 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Destination details never probed — only the 75104 zip; no stairs, floors, parking, or access at the Cedar Hill end
Never probed boxes, storage stops, additional stops, garage/storage/balcony rooms, packing services, or moving stressors
Did not challenge the 1-bedroom / '2200' square-foot mismatch, and at 2200 sqft never raised the virtual walkthrough path
Used the customer's name only once (to confirm it off caller ID), never again in the call
top_strength: Genuinely honest and customer-first at the moment of disqualification — he told Dani straight out that Einstein doesn't move baby grands rather than fudging it, then proactively coached her on what to ask other movers (materials, gas fee, credit card fee, 'make sure the quote includes everything you'd be billed for'). That is real integrity and it left the customer thanking him.
coaching_note: The piano was not a reason to end the call — it was a reason to carve out one item. Dani said her sister was packing most of it herself and only the baby grand was a problem; Landon even told her to call back if she found someone for the piano. The right move was to say 'we can't take the grand, but I can quote you everything else right now,' then run the full pricing, clock, estimate, and Save Your Ass sections and try to lock the Wednesday the 16th slot he had already confirmed was open. He effectively referred out a bookable one-bedroom Richardson-to-Cedar Hill move. Second, at a stated ~2200 sqft this should have been surfaced as a virtual walkthrough candidate, and the 1-bedroom / 2200 sqft mismatch should have been resolved before any quote.
phone_presence_notes: Friendly and easy to talk to, but the warmth ran through repeated filler ('awesome, awesome, awesome', 'of course, of course') rather than personalized engagement — he never used Dani's name after confirming it and never acknowledged the letdown of turning her sister's move away.
audio_review_reason: Heavy disfluency and garbled passages throughout the transcript ('I pro, if you don't totally understandable', 'moving the Baan', 'Let me bring it at all to', 'recommend recommend') — needs audio to tell whether this is a transcription artifact or a genuine clarity and pacing problem worth coaching.
